changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For marketplace and low-ticket prospects whose pain is operational rather than lost revenue, stop presenting the acceptance-rate slide in first calls. Spend that time on getting their providers paid locally and on freeing up their engineers. Keep M4 for buyers who raise authorization rates themselves.
changes.why: The rep presented the acceptance-rate slide in full and got 'Silence', and the decider dismissed it outright with 'our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates.'

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For gig and service apps, use the buyer's words: 'Payments shouldn't be a team: get your sitters paid locally in every country you launch.' Swap 'sitters' for the prospect's own word for its providers. Say 'sitter pay', not 'payouts', and 'the app', not 'marketplace'. Only add a timing promise in the 'paid by Friday' style after we have confirmed we can meet it.
changes.why: The marketplace capabilities landed (E20), but the customer describes them as 'sitter pay' and 'paid by Friday' and wants payments not to be a team, while our line uses the category words they never say.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For engineering-led marketplace deals, open with the cost of running payments in-house instead of global growth: 'Stop babysitting your payments. Get your engineers back and ship the roadmap items payments keeps pushing.' Then present local-currency payouts as the way they launch new countries.
changes.why: Expansion was the occasion (E1), but the pain the customer described was two engineers 'more or less full-time just keeping sitter payments working', a faster-pay roadmap item 'pushed three quarters in a row', and wanting to 'stop babysitting this.'

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Keep the developer line, but end it with a call to action for the prospect's engineers: 'Build your own sitter pay flow in our sandbox before you decide.' Adapt 'sitter pay' to the prospect's use case. Make inviting that hands-on build a planned step in the sales motion, aimed at the engineering decider's team.
changes.why: The docs and sandbox landed, and the deal turned when an engineer built 'a working sitter payment flow over a weekend', after which 'Daniel stopped saying 'if''. The decider was engineering, but nothing in our motion invited or tracked that build.
